title: Anti-Adalimumab Antibodies in Children With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and/or Chronic Non-Infectious Uveitis
off: Anti-Adalimumab Antibodies in a Prospective Cohort of Patients With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and/or Chronic Non-Infectious Uveitis: Incidence, Predictive Factors, and Clinical Correlations
summary:
This prospective, single-center observational cohort study aims to investigate the development of anti-Adalimumab antibodies in pediatric patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and/or chronic non-infectious uveitis initiating Adalimumab treatment.

The study will assess the frequency and timing of antibody development, identify potential predictive factors, including concomitant methotrexate treatment, and explore associations between immunogenicity, serum Adalimumab concentrations, disease activity, and clinical outcomes.

A total of 60 patients will be enrolled and followed for 24 months. Clinical data and additional blood samples will be collected at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months during routine clinical visits.

Anti-Adalimumab antibodies and serum drug concentrations will be measured using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology. Treatment decisions will remain entirely based on routine clinical practice.
desc:
Adalimumab is widely used in the treatment of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and chronic non-infectious uveitis. Despite its established efficacy, some patients experience inadequate clinical response, secondary loss of efficacy, or disease flares during treatment. The development of anti-Adalimumab antibodies (AAA) may contribute to reduced serum drug concentrations and impaired therapeutic response. However, evidence regarding the incidence, timing, and clinical significance of AAA in paediatric patients remains limited and heterogeneous.

This prospective, single-centre, observational cohort study aims to investigate the development and kinetics of AAA in paediatric patients with JIA and/or chronic non-infectious uveitis initiating Adalimumab treatment. The study will also explore potential predictive factors for AAA development, including concomitant methotrexate therapy, and evaluate associations between immunogenicity, serum Adalimumab concentrations, disease activity, and clinical outcomes.

A total of 60 Adalimumab-naïve patients will be consecutively enrolled at AOU Meyer IRCCS, Florence, Italy. All participants will receive Adalimumab according to routine clinical practice, independently of study participation. No investigational treatment or study-related therapeutic intervention is planned.

Each participant will be followed for 24 months, with assessments at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. Clinical and laboratory data will be collected during routine follow-up visits, including demographic characteristics, disease subtype and duration, concomitant treatments, disease activity measures, inflammatory markers, disease flares, and treatment modifications.

At each scheduled assessment, an additional 5 mL peripheral blood sample will be collected during routine blood sampling. Serum samples will be analysed at the PeptLab laboratory of the University of Florence using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology to determine AAA positivity and levels, as well as serum Adalimumab concentrations. AAA positivity will be defined according to a predefined threshold of 15 Response Units (RU).

The primary outcomes are the proportion of patients developing AAA during follow-up and the time from Adalimumab initiation to the first detection of AAA. Secondary outcomes include the identification of clinical and treatment-related factors associated with AAA development, changes in disease activity and functional assessment scores (JADAS-10 and CHAQ), inflammatory markers, occurrence and number of disease flares, and persistence of AAA positivity.

Statistical analyses will include descriptive and exploratory multivariable methods, longitudinal models for repeated measurements, and time-to-event analyses accounting for interval censoring when appropriate. Particular attention will be given to the potential association between concomitant methotrexate treatment and AAA development.

The overall study duration is expected to be 72 months, including 36 months of recruitment, individual follow-up, and final data analysis and reporting.

The study aims to improve understanding of Adalimumab immunogenicity in paediatric JIA and chronic non-infectious uveitis and to explore the potential clinical value of immunopharmacological monitoring in identifying patients at risk of secondary treatment failure or disease relapse.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

Age at diagnosis between 2 and 16 years.

Diagnosis of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) according to the International League of Associations for Rheumatology (ILAR) criteria, established on or after January 1, 2015, and/or diagnosis of chronic non-infectious uveitis according to the Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature (SUN) Working Group criteria, established on or after January 1, 2015.

Clinical indication to initiate Adalimumab treatment in patients with no previous exposure to Adalimumab (Adalimumab-naïve), as determined by the treating physician.

Written informed consent from parents or legal guardians and assent from minors aged 7 years or older, where applicable.

Exclusion Criteria:

Age 18 years or older at enrollment.

Diagnoses other than juvenile idiopathic arthritis or chronic non-infectious uveitis.

Contraindications to Adalimumab, including tuberculosis exposure, history of multiple sclerosis or other demyelinating central nervous system disorders, or history of malignancy.

Previous exposure to Adalimumab before study enrollment.

Body weight below 12 kg.

Age below 24 months at enrollment.

arms.l: Adalimumab-treated patients with JIA and/or chronic non-infectious uveitis
arms.d:
Pediatric patients diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and/or chronic non-infectious uveitis who are initiating Adalimumab treatment according to routine clinical practice and have not previously received Adalimumab.

Patients will be prospectively followed for 24 months, with clinical assessments and blood sample collection at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months to evaluate the development of anti-Adalimumab antibodies, serum drug concentrations, and clinical outcomes.

x.titre: Anticorps anti-adalimumab chez l'enfant atteint d'arthrite juvénile ou d'uvéite chronique
x.question: Quelle proportion d'enfants développe des anticorps anti-adalimumab, et à quel moment, après le début du traitement ?
x.contexte:
L'adalimumab, anti-TNF, est très utilisé dans l'arthrite juvénile idiopathique (AJI) et dans l'uvéite chronique non infectieuse de l'enfant, notamment en cas d'échec du méthotrexate. Une partie des enfants présente une réponse insuffisante, une perte de réponse secondaire ou des poussées sous traitement.

La formation d'anticorps anti-adalimumab peut abaisser les concentrations sériques du médicament et réduire son efficacité. Les données pédiatriques sur la fréquence, le délai d'apparition et la portée clinique de ces anticorps restent limitées et hétérogènes.

Le méthotrexate associé pourrait réduire l'immunogénicité, comme chez l'adulte, mais cela est mal établi chez l'enfant. Le dosage des concentrations et des anticorps pourrait aider à repérer les patients à risque d'échec secondaire ou de rechute.

Cette cohorte observationnelle monocentrique de l'hôpital pédiatrique Meyer (Florence, Italie) suivra 60 enfants naïfs d'adalimumab pendant 24 mois. Des prélèvements sanguins supplémentaires de 5 mL sont réalisés à l'inclusion et à 3, 6, 12, 18 et 24 mois, lors des visites habituelles. Les anticorps et la concentration d'adalimumab sont mesurés par résonance plasmonique de surface, avec un seuil de positivité de 15 unités de réponse. Le traitement reste décidé selon la pratique courante.
x.interet: Les résultats préciseront à quelle fréquence et à quel moment l'immunogénicité survient chez l'enfant, et le rôle du méthotrexate associé. Ils pourraient justifier un suivi pharmacologique systématique de l'adalimumab dans l'AJI et l'uvéite.
x.profil: Des enfants de 2 à 17 ans atteints d'AJI et/ou d'uvéite chronique non infectieuse, qui débutent l'adalimumab.
inclusion: Diagnostic d'AJI (critères ILAR) et/ou d'uvéite chronique non infectieuse (critères SUN) posé depuis le 1er janvier 2015
Âge au diagnostic entre 2 et 16 ans
Indication d'adalimumab posée par le médecin, sans exposition antérieure
Consentement écrit des parents ou tuteurs et assentiment des enfants de 7 ans et plus
exclusion: Âge ≥ 18 ans à l'inclusion ou < 24 mois
Autre diagnostic que l'AJI ou l'uvéite chronique non infectieuse
Contre-indication à l'adalimumab (tuberculose, maladie démyélinisante, antécédent de cancer)

bras.traitement: Adalimumab débuté selon la pratique courante, avec prélèvements sanguins supplémentaires à l'inclusion puis à 3, 6, 12, 18 et 24 mois

x.critere: Proportion d'enfants développant des anticorps anti-adalimumab et délai jusqu'à leur première détection, jusqu'à 24 mois
